shower.thought: We spend our whole lives looking for things we've lost, but we never stop to think about how many things we've lost that we never even knew we had.
The people you've forgotten about have probably forgotten about you too, and that mutual erasure might be the closest thing we have to true forgiveness.
You can't remember what it felt like to not know something, so you can't actually measure how much you've learned.

Somewhere right now, someone is having the worst day of their life while you're complaining about something trivial, and somewhere else, someone would trade their worst day for your trivial problem without hesitation.
Nostalgia is just grief wearing a prettier mask.
The most honest thing anyone says is usually something they didn't mean to say out loud.
You've been a different person multiple times in your life, but nobody threw you a funeral for the versions that died.
When you daydream about being confident, you're already being confident—you're just doing it in a scenario where nobody's watching.
The things you're most ashamed of are often the most relatable, which is why people bond over them so deeply.
If you've ever laughed at your own joke alone, you've experienced what it's like to be two different people having a conversation.
We call it "overthinking" when we're trying to understand ourselves, but "wisdom" when we're trying to understand others.
Regret is just a conversation with a version of yourself who made a different choice.
The scariest part of getting older isn't that things hurt more—it's that you care less about things that once felt like they'd destroy you.
You're probably someone's "remember them?" story right now, and you'll never know it.
Death is the one deadline that doesn't come with a warning email, but you treat every other deadline like it might.
The people you see every day slowly become invisible to you, not because you stop noticing them, but because you notice them so much that your brain stops processing them as new information.
Confidence is just stubbornness that worked out.
Your second-guessing yourself is proof that you're capable of thinking critically, but you only call it that when it's about other people.
We're terrified of being forgotten, but we're equally terrified of being truly known.
The most productive thing you did today might have been thinking about doing something tomorrow.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.

My therapist asked what I wanted to get out of our sessions.
I said, "Out of here." She said that's $150.
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.

My dentist told me I need to floss more.
I said, "You're right, I should take better care of things I neglect."

I asked my friend how his new antidepressants were working.
He said, "Great! I don't even remember why I was sad anymore."

People keep asking if I'm okay.
Apparently, nodding while crying sends mixed signals.

I tried to tell my kids about the good old days.
They said, "Okay boomer," and I realized they were right—I should be dead by now.

My wife asked if I was seeing someone else.
I said, "Only when she's in the room."

The worst part about having social anxiety is meeting new people.
The best part is having a perfect excuse to avoid literally everyone.

I told my Alexa I was depressed.
She suggested shopping. Amazon really does know me.

My doctor said I need to cut back on drinking.
I said, "You're right, I'll switch to beer." He's not my doctor anymore.

I got fired from the calendar factory.
Apparently, taking a day off was unacceptable.

My therapist told me to practice self-love.
I've been doing great until I realized I'm just narcissistic.

I asked my parents why they had me.
They said, "Honestly, the condom broke." At least I know I was a surprise—to them too.

My friend said he's been on a seafood diet.
I said, "That's great, you must look amazing." He said, "No, I see food and I eat it." Then he ate my lunch.

I told my boss I was thinking about quitting.
He said, "Please do." Turns out he was already thinking about it.

My kid asked why people die.
I said, "So we have a reason to go to family reunions eventually."

I started a support group for people with short-term memory loss.
We haven't met yet because I forgot to schedule it. Last week, I forgot again. Next week, I'm definitely going to remember to forget.

My date asked what my most embarrassing moment was.
I said, "I'm living it right now." She's blocked me on everything.

I told my accountant I wanted to hide money from my wife.
He said, "I'd suggest a good divorce lawyer." Smart man—saved me a lot of money.
